judges: Narendra Kumar Vyas Cav Judgment J.
trial_court: Second Civil Judge, Class-II, Champa District Janjgir Champa in Civil Suit No. 48 A/2008
case_name: Vijay Kumar Pandey vs Chameli Bai And Anr
facts_of_case: The plaintiff filed a suit for declaration of title contending that the property as ancestral property. The trial court dismissed the suit.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the plaintiff to substantiate his stand.
legal_principles.held: The plaintiff to substantiate his stand has examined Vijay Kumar Pandey (PW-1), Girish Kumar (PW-2), Heeralal (Ex.P-3) and exhibited documents as adoption deed (Ex.P-1) dated 19.12.1986, Panchanama order (Ex.P-2), B-1 Kistbandi (Ex.P-3), B-1 Kistbandi (Ex.P-4), Khasra panchasala (Ex.P-5).

legal_principles.principle: The court will not accept a document as genuine unless it is proved to be so.
legal_principles.held: He has also admitted that in adoption deed (Ex.P-1) Kamla Bai and Chameli Bai have put their signatures. He has also admitted that after death of Heeralal, names of Chameli Bai and Kamla Bai have been mutated in the revenue records.

outcome.final_order: Whether the learned trial Court was justified in dismissing the suit filed by the plaintiff ignoring the well settled legal position that the second wife cannot inherent ancestral property of her husband ignoring the provisions of Hindu Succession Act?
